runtime: Expo Go development over USB, Metro 8083 offline
protocol: One initial Paneer warm-up (8838ms), then normal Paneer, blocked Paneer, blocked Butter, normal Butter. Same app/source, no restart or edits during trials. LowP query cache reset before each request through existing concurrency-count control. Website caches/cookies retained; native result thumbnails retained. CDP attached in both conditions. No UI dump during loading. Four warm searches, exploratory only, no statistical speedup claim.

imageBlocking.method: CDP Fetch.enable resourceType Image, failRequest BlockedByClient; temporary development-only, disabled after test.
imageBlocking.limitations: Memory-cached images bypass interception. Baseline Paneer primed image caches, so Paneer is weak evidence. Counters are cumulative across BOTH blocked trials.

apiTimelineNormalButter.clock: Navigation-relative Resource Timing. Zepto/Swiggy/Blinkit endpoint names inspected locally; queries, headers, cookies and bodies not exported.

conclusions: No consistent image-blocking speed gain: Paneer -84ms; Butter +424ms.
LowP scan work is tens of milliseconds; larger costs precede extraction: website startup, requests and rendering, plus concurrency queueing.
This does not separate all CPU time from network/async waits; long-task durations are partial observations, not CPU profiles.
All five stores returned candidates in each trial. Product/SKU correctness is not established, especially Flipkart's paneer-herb/peanut-butter alternatives.
No app behavior or default changed from this experiment.
